gen-dafont-cheri-fs-bespoke-slab: Sturdy, friendly script with no thin hairlines at all. Bespoke Slab follows as a classic serif with tall bodies, made for short stretches of reading that still feel grounded.
gen-dafont-college-gf-abeezee: Authoritative in its tall, wide-countered lowercase, College gets a friendly partner in ABeeZee, whose sans terminals finish well clear of the stem. That openness is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-college-gf-aldrich: Chunky, confident capitals and tall lowercase up top. Aldrich's sans-serif letters sit close to cap height and look cupped rather than clenched, so they sit beside College's heavy curves like a thinner thread beside a rope.
gen-dafont-college-gf-alexandria: Curves as heavy as its straight stems give College a blocky, dynamic punch, and Alexandria answers underneath with a sans that is lower and wide at the c opening, letting the heading take the weight.
gen-dafont-college-gf-amiko: Dynamic, through and through. Amiko's sans terminals flare outward like tongs, so its lighter strokes make a lively counterpoint to College's uniformly heavy ones.
gen-dafont-college-gf-anek-bangla: College hits hard with uniform strokes and no downstroke swell. Anek Bangla sits beneath it as a sans with wide, barely curled s shapes, lower and lighter, so the heading owns the emphasis.
gen-dafont-college-gf-anek-devanagari: Authoritative and tall-lowercased, College builds every letter from a single stroke width, while Anek Devanagari keeps a plain sans body with distinctly open mouths. Their difference in weight does the work.
gen-dafont-college-gf-anek-gujarati: Anek Gujarati reads as a sans with lowercase that rivals its capitals and a gaping c. And College's wire-like monoline skeleton gives it a heading with real stand-out force.
gen-dafont-college-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Plain, unshaded lines that never swell define College's authoritative heading. And Anek Gurmukhi follows in a lighter sans-serif, its big open counters making long paragraphs feel easy to move through.
gen-dafont-college-gf-anek-kannada: Cable-like, unswelling lines in a tall lowercase. Anek Kannada then takes over as a sans-serif with a high x-height and terminals that stop far from the stem, which leaves College to carry the weight.
